$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Cloud Scheduler. One entry per console section; level per substrate (nano = shared core, also dev_server/unified ingress; offline = appliance). Proven by tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py — a claim the backend does not honour fails CI.

gcp.cloudscheduler.jobs.schedule.title: Pause, resume and force run
limitations: Schedules are advanced lazily on read/run, not by a background timer: a due job fires the first time any request touches its project (list, get or run), not at the exact wall-clock instant.
A missed tick is never replayed — only the single next occurrence is computed.

gcp.cloudscheduler.jobs.targets.title: HTTP, Pub/Sub and App Engine HTTP targets
limitations: A Pub/Sub target is delivered into Vyomi's Pub/Sub core for real — a subscriber receives an actual message.
HTTP and App Engine HTTP targets are recorded as attempted (lastAttemptTime/status are stamped); Vyomi makes no outbound network call, so the target URL is never actually invoked.
OAuth and OIDC auth headers are stored and returned to the SDK exactly as configured but are not verified or used to sign an outbound request.

gcp.cloudscheduler.cron-jobs.title: App Engine cron jobs (legacy cron.yaml)
limitations: App Engine isn't modeled in Vyomi, so the legacy cron.yaml-based jobs the real console lists under this tab have no backend to read from.
